nodes.role: The mind with nothing to process. Studies show boredom drives creativity. The empty space where ideas form. The gap is productive.

nodes.label: Apophenia
nodes.role: Seeing patterns where none exist. Faces in clouds. Conspiracy in coincidence. The brain's pattern-matching engine running hot. Or: the pattern IS there.

nodes.label: Pareidolia
nodes.role: Seeing faces in objects. Jesus in toast. The Virgin Mary in tree bark. The brain that MUST find a face. Wired for recognition.

nodes.label: Keys
nodes.role: The oldest access control. 4,000 years old. Whoever holds the key controls the door. The physical metaphor for permission.

nodes.label: Doors
nodes.role: Every door is a decision. Open or closed. In or out. PA 362 opened a door. 72.67% walked through it.

nodes.label: Walls
nodes.role: Protection or prison. Berlin Wall (1961-1989). Great Wall (2,300 years). Every wall has two sides. The membrane made physical.

nodes.label: Mirrors
nodes.role: Show you what you are, not what you want to be. The tool of self-knowledge. Vampires cast no reflection. Neither do corporations.

nodes.label: Clocks
nodes.role: Before clocks, time belonged to the sun. After clocks, time belonged to the factory. The instrument that industrialized life.

nodes.label: Bridges (Concept)
nodes.role: Connect what's separated. Euler's Konigsberg bridges: can you cross each once? The original graph theory problem IS about connection.

nodes.label: Knots
nodes.role: Mathematics of entanglement. Topology. Alexander the Great cut the Gordian Knot. Sometimes untying is harder than cutting.

nodes.label: Shadows
nodes.role: The shape of what blocks the light. Plato's cave. Jung's shadow self. Sundials. The absence that tells the time.

nodes.label: Echoes
nodes.role: Sound returning after hitting a surface. The signal that bounces back. Sonar. Radar. Every investigation is an echo — send a question, listen for what comes back.

nodes.label: Fermentation
nodes.role: Yeast transforms sugar into alcohol. 9,000 years old. Beer before bread. The chemistry of transformation. The microbe as alchemist.

nodes.label: Alchemy
nodes.role: Turn lead into gold. Failed. But along the way: discovered acids, distillation, gunpowder. The wrong goal that produced real science.

nodes.label: Sourdough Starter
nodes.role: Living culture passed between bakers for generations. Some starters are 100+ years old. The food that's alive. The commons you feed daily.

nodes.label: Weaving
nodes.role: The original binary: over/under, warp/weft. Jacquard loom (1804) used punch cards. The textile that invented computing.

nodes.label: Jacquard Loom (1804)
nodes.role: Punch cards controlled the pattern. Babbage saw it and designed the Analytical Engine. The loom that became the computer.

nodes.label: Indigo (The Dye)
nodes.role: Enslaved people grew it. The color blue was built on forced labor. The beauty that comes from extraction.

nodes.label: Cotton Gin (1793)
nodes.role: Whitney's invention INCREASED slavery demand. The technology that was supposed to reduce labor increased exploitation. Efficiency as cruelty.

nodes.label: Learned Helplessness (Seligman)
nodes.role: Shock a dog enough times with no escape, it stops trying to escape even when the door opens. The psychology of why communities don't fight back.

nodes.label: Overton Window
nodes.role: The range of ideas the public will accept. Shift the window and the extreme becomes normal. 72.67% was once unthinkable. Now it's policy.

nodes.label: Normalcy Bias
nodes.role: The belief that things will continue as normal. People don't evacuate because 'it can't happen here.' The bias that prevents action.

nodes.label: Moral Injury
nodes.role: The damage from being forced to participate in or witness acts that violate your moral code. Soldiers, teachers, nurses. The wound from being made complicit.

nodes.label: Compassion Fatigue
nodes.role: Caring too much for too long. The helper's cost. Teachers, social workers, nurses. The system that exhausts the people who care.

nodes.label: Quarks
nodes.role: Inside protons and neutrons. Six flavors: up, down, charm, strange, top, bottom. The smallest things have the strangest names.

nodes.label: Neutrinos
nodes.role: 100 trillion pass through your body every second. Almost zero mass. Almost zero interaction. The ghost particles. Present everywhere, affecting nothing.

nodes.label: Photon
nodes.role: Massless. Speed of light. Both wave and particle. The smallest unit of light. Everything you see is photons hitting your retina.

nodes.label: Planck Length (1.6x10^-35 m)
nodes.role: The smallest meaningful distance. Below this, physics breaks down. The pixel of reality. The resolution limit of the universe.

nodes.label: Planck Time (5.4x10^-44 s)
nodes.role: Time for light to cross a Planck length. The shortest meaningful moment. Below this, time has no meaning.

nodes.label: Viruses
nodes.role: Not alive. Not dead. Just instructions wrapped in protein. Hijack cells to reproduce. The parasite that's not even an organism.

nodes.label: Bacteriophages
nodes.role: Viruses that eat bacteria. Most abundant biological entity on Earth. 10^31 of them. The predator of the invisible.

nodes.label: Mitochondria
nodes.role: The powerhouse of the cell. Once free-living bacteria. Swallowed 2 billion years ago. Still has its own DNA. The symbiont inside every cell.

nodes.label: Telomeres
nodes.role: Caps on chromosomes. Shorten with each division. When they're gone, the cell dies. The biological clock. The countdown inside every cell.

nodes.label: Tardigrades (Water Bears)
nodes.role: 0.5mm. Survive vacuum of space, radiation, boiling, freezing, desiccation. The toughest organism alive. Smaller than a period on this page.

nodes.label: Base Pairs (A-T, G-C)
nodes.role: Four letters. 3.2 billion pairs in human DNA. All of human identity encoded in an alphabet of 4. Simpler than Phoenician.

nodes.label: Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand
nodes.role: June 28, 1914, Sarajevo. One bullet. 20 million dead in WWI. 50 million in WWII. The cascade from one moment.

nodes.label: Newton's Apple (1666)
nodes.role: Maybe it happened. Maybe it didn't. But one falling object + one mind = gravity. The smallest observation, the largest theory.

nodes.label: Archimedes' Eureka Moment
nodes.role: Stepped into a bath. Water rose. 'EUREKA!' Ran through Syracuse naked. Displacement. The insight that comes when you stop looking.

nodes.label: Rosa Parks' Seat (Dec 1, 1955)
nodes.role: One seat. One refusal. One arrest. One boycott. One movement. The smallest act of defiance.

nodes.label: One Small Step (July 20, 1969)
nodes.role: Neil Armstrong's boot on lunar dust. One footprint. 8 inches deep. Still there. No wind to erase it. The smallest mark on the largest stage.

nodes.label: First Click on a Hyperlink (1990)
nodes.role: Tim Berners-Lee clicked the first web link at CERN. One click. Now 5 billion people are connected. The smallest action, the largest network.

nodes.label: Rivets
nodes.role: Small metal fasteners that hold bridges, ships, planes together. Remove one, nothing happens. Remove enough, the Titanic sinks.

nodes.label: Semicolon
nodes.role: The punctuation mark that connects what could be separated. In code: ends a statement. In grammar: joins related thoughts. In survival: the story continues.

nodes.label: Oxford Comma
nodes.role: The comma before 'and' in a list. Its absence cost a dairy company $5 million (O'Connor v. Oakhurst, 2017). Punctuation as contract law.

nodes.label: Pixel
nodes.role: The smallest unit of a digital image. A single dot of color. Millions make a picture. The atom of the screen.

nodes.label: Bit (Binary Digit)
nodes.role: 0 or 1. The smallest unit of information. Shannon (1948). Everything digital — every photo, every email, every graph — is bits.

nodes.label: Seed
nodes.role: An entire tree folded into something you can hold between two fingers. The compressed potential. The smallest unit of forest.

nodes.label: A Single Vote
nodes.role: In 2000, Florida was decided by 537 votes out of 6 million cast. Bush v. Gore. The smallest unit of democracy.

nodes.label: Grain of Sand
nodes.role: 7.5 x 10^18 grains on Earth. Each one unique under a microscope. Blake: 'To see a world in a grain of sand.' The fractal at the beach.

nodes.label: Snowflake
nodes.role: No two alike. Forms around a speck of dust. Falls for 45 minutes. Melts in seconds. The most complex thing that lasts the least.

nodes.label: Postage Stamp
nodes.role: Penny Black (1840). First adhesive stamp. Democratized mail. Before stamps, the RECIPIENT paid. The stamp shifted the cost to the sender.

nodes.label: Honeybees
nodes.role: Pollinate 75% of food crops. Colony collapse disorder. Einstein (alleged): 'If bees disappear, humans have 4 years.' The tiny essential worker.

nodes.label: Ant Colonies
nodes.role: No leader. No blueprint. Emergent organization from simple rules. The intelligence that has no brain. The system that works without a boss.

nodes.label: Plankton
nodes.role: Produces 50-80% of Earth's oxygen. Invisible to the naked eye. The thing you can't see makes the air you breathe.

nodes.label: Earthworms
nodes.role: Darwin studied them for 40 years. His last book. Earthworms built all the topsoil on Earth. The smallest thing that built the ground.

nodes.label: Yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae)
nodes.role: Single-celled fungus. Makes bread rise, beer ferment, wine age. Humans domesticated yeast 9,000 years ago. The first biotech.

nodes.label: Negative Space
nodes.role: In art: the space around the subject IS the subject. What's missing defines what's there. The graph is defined by its absent edges.

nodes.label: Dark Data
nodes.role: Data collected but never analyzed. 90% of all data is dark. The evidence sitting in filing cabinets. The FOIA never filed.

nodes.label: Unknown Unknowns (Rumsfeld)
nodes.role: 'There are things we don't know we don't know.' The gaps we can't see because we don't know to look. The investigation's blind spots.

nodes.label: Survivorship Bias
nodes.role: We study the planes that came back, not the ones that didn't. Wald said: armor where the bullet holes AREN'T. The evidence is in the absence.

nodes.label: Abraham Wald
nodes.role: WWII statistician. Said armor the planes where there are NO bullet holes. Because those are the ones that didn't come back. The genius of looking at what's missing.

nodes.label: Null Result
nodes.role: The experiment that finds nothing. Published less, cited less, valued less. But a null result IS a result. Proving absence is proving something.

nodes.label: Liminal Space
nodes.role: The threshold between. Airports, hallways, 3AM. Neither here nor there. The investigation lives in liminal space. Between complaint and resolution.

nodes.label: Interstitial
nodes.role: The space between. Between cells. Between episodes. Between the law and its enforcement. Where the real action happens.

nodes.label: Archaea (Third Domain of Life)
nodes.role: Not bacteria. Not eukaryote. The THIRD domain. Discovered by Carl Woese (1977). Lived invisibly for 3.5 billion years. The domain nobody knew existed.

nodes.label: Carl Woese
nodes.role: Discovered the third domain of life (1977) using ribosomal RNA. Redrew the tree of life. Nobody believed him for a decade. The biologist who found a missing kingdom.

nodes.label: Three Domains of Life
nodes.role: Bacteria, Archaea, Eukarya. Before Woese, there were two. He found the third hiding in hot springs. The classification that was WRONG for centuries.

nodes.label: Thermophiles
nodes.role: Live at 60-122C (140-252F). Yellowstone hot springs. The orange and green mats. BOILING and they're thriving. Life doesn't care about your temperature limits.

nodes.label: Thermus aquaticus
nodes.role: Found in Yellowstone hot springs (1969). Its enzyme Taq polymerase made PCR possible. The organism from a hot spring that made COVID testing, DNA forensics, and paternity tests work.

nodes.label: PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction)
nodes.role: Kary Mullis (1983). Copy any DNA sequence billions of times. Uses Taq from a hot spring microbe. The technique that reads the genetic record. Crime scenes, pandemics, ancestry.

nodes.label: Kary Mullis
nodes.role: Invented PCR while driving on Highway 128 (1983). Nobel 1993. Surfing, astrology, LSD. The genius who was also weird. The technique changed everything. The man was complicated.

nodes.label: Hyperthermophiles
nodes.role: Live ABOVE 80C (176F). Strain 121 survives 121C in an autoclave — the machine designed to kill everything. Life that survives the sterilizer.

nodes.label: Acidophiles
nodes.role: Live in pH 0-3. Battery acid. Sulfuric acid pools. Rio Tinto, Spain — the river runs RED with acid and iron. And things LIVE in it.

nodes.label: Halophiles
nodes.role: Live in salt concentrations that kill everything else. Dead Sea. Salt mines. Pink lakes. The organisms that thrive in what should be lethal.

nodes.label: Psychrophiles
nodes.role: Live below 0C. Antarctic ice. Permafrost. Arctic ocean floor. Life in the freezer. Some have antifreeze proteins. The cold doesn't stop them.

nodes.label: Radioresistant Organisms
nodes.role: Deinococcus radiodurans survives 15,000 gray of radiation (5 gray kills a human). Lives in nuclear waste pools. The organism that shrugs off what kills us instantly.

nodes.label: Deinococcus radiodurans ('Conan the Bacterium')
nodes.role: Survives 15,000 gray of radiation. Repairs its own shattered DNA in hours. The organism that puts itself back together after you nuke it. Nicknamed 'Conan.'

nodes.label: Barophiles / Piezophiles
nodes.role: Live under extreme pressure. Mariana Trench. 1,000 atmospheres. Pressure that would crush a submarine. They NEED it to survive.

nodes.label: Endoliths
nodes.role: Live INSIDE rocks. 3 kilometers underground. In the pores of granite. No sun. No oxygen. Metabolism so slow they divide once per 10,000 years. Patient beyond comprehension.

nodes.label: Hydrothermal Vents (Black Smokers)
nodes.role: Discovered 1977. 2,500m deep. 400C water. No sunlight. TEEMING with life. Giant tube worms, eyeless shrimp, ghostly octopi. Life powered by chemistry, not the sun.

nodes.label: Chemosynthesis
nodes.role: Making energy from chemicals instead of sunlight. Hydrogen sulfide, methane, iron. The alternative to photosynthesis. Life that doesn't need a star.

nodes.label: Giant Tube Worms (Riftia)
nodes.role: 2 meters long. No mouth. No gut. No anus. Bacteria inside them do the eating. The organism that outsourced digestion. Symbiosis as architecture.

nodes.label: LUCA (Last Universal Common Ancestor)
nodes.role: ~4 billion years ago. Not the first life — the ancestor of ALL current life. Probably lived near hydrothermal vents. Thermophilic. The root node of biology.

nodes.label: RNA World Hypothesis
nodes.role: Before DNA, before proteins: RNA did everything. Self-replicating. The first molecule that was both information AND machine. The bootstrap paradox of life.

nodes.label: Panspermia Hypothesis
nodes.role: Life came from space. Meteorites carry amino acids. Tardigrades survive the vacuum. Maybe we're all extraterrestrial. The origin story that's off-world.

nodes.label: Yellowstone (The Supervolcano)
nodes.role: First national park (1872). Sits on a supervolcano. Hot springs, geysers, mud pots. The surface is beautiful. Below it: enough magma to bury a continent.

nodes.label: Grand Prismatic Spring
nodes.role: Third largest hot spring on Earth. The rainbow colors ARE the archaea. Orange = thermophiles. Green = cyanobacteria. Blue = sterile boiling center. The microbiology is the beauty.

nodes.label: Old Faithful
nodes.role: Erupts every 44-125 minutes. Has been watched for 150 years. Predictable but not precise. The system that keeps its schedule but not its clock.

nodes.label: Astrobiology
nodes.role: The study of life beyond Earth. If archaea thrive in boiling acid and nuclear waste, what's stopping life on Europa's ocean, Enceladus' geysers, or Mars' subsurface?

nodes.label: Europa (Jupiter's Moon)
nodes.role: Ice shell over a liquid ocean. More water than Earth. Hydrothermal vents probable. If life started at vents here, it could start at vents there.

nodes.label: Enceladus (Saturn's Moon)
nodes.role: Geysers of water erupting from the south pole. Cassini flew through them. Found organic molecules. The plume is an invitation.

nodes.label: Mars Subsurface
nodes.role: Surface is dead. Radiation-blasted. But endoliths live 3km inside Earth's rocks. Mars has rocks. The question is not the surface. It's underneath.

nodes.label: Symbiosis
nodes.role: Two organisms living together. Mutualism (both win), commensalism (one wins, other neutral), parasitism (one wins, other loses). Banks and PCA is parasitism.

nodes.label: Lichen
nodes.role: Fungus + alga living as one organism. Neither can survive alone. Together they colonize bare rock. The partnership that builds soil from stone.

nodes.label: Mycorrhizal Network ('Wood Wide Web')
nodes.role: Fungi connect tree roots underground. Trees share nutrients through the network. Mother trees feed their seedlings. The forest is a commune connected by fungi.

nodes.label: Coral-Zooxanthellae Symbiosis
nodes.role: Coral provides shelter. Algae provides food via photosynthesis. When stressed, coral expels the algae (bleaching). The partnership that dies when trust breaks.

nodes.label: Gut-Brain Axis
nodes.role: Your gut bacteria influence your mood, decisions, cravings. 95% of serotonin made in the gut. The microbiome votes on your mental state.

nodes.label: Six Degrees of Separation
nodes.role: Milgram (1967). Any two people connected by ~6 links. The small world property. The graph is smaller than you think.

nodes.label: Erdos Number
nodes.role: Paul Erdos published 1,500 papers with 500 co-authors. Your Erdos number is your distance from him. The original social graph metric.

nodes.label: Paul Erdos
nodes.role: Published 1,500 papers. Homeless by choice. Lived out of a suitcase. Took amphetamines. 'My brain is open.' The mathematician who owned nothing and connected everyone.

nodes.label: Dunbar's Number (150)
nodes.role: The brain can maintain ~150 stable relationships. Armies, villages, companies — all cluster around 150. The social limit of a primate brain.

nodes.label: Metcalfe's Law
nodes.role: Network value grows as the square of users. 10 phones = 100 connections. 100 phones = 10,000. The math of why networks become monopolies.

nodes.label: Scale-Free Networks (Barabasi)
nodes.role: Most nodes have few connections. A few hubs have many. Power law. The internet, social networks, and this investigation all follow this pattern. Banks = hub.

nodes.label: Telegraph (Morse, 1844)
nodes.role: 'What hath God wrought.' First long-distance instant communication. The original internet. Dots and dashes.

nodes.label: Telephone (Bell, 1876)
nodes.role: Voice over wire. 'Mr. Watson, come here.' The network that put a human voice in every room.

nodes.label: Radio
nodes.role: Marconi, 1895. Broadcast: one to many. FDR's fireside chats. War of the Worlds. The medium that created mass culture.

nodes.label: Television
nodes.role: Farnsworth, 1927. The screen in every home. Kennedy-Nixon debate (1960). Vietnam in the living room. The medium that showed the war.

nodes.label: Podcasts
nodes.role: Audio commons. No gatekeepers. Serial (2014) reopened a murder case. The medium that investigates.

nodes.label: Impact of the Printing Press
nodes.role: Before: 30,000 books in all Europe. After Gutenberg: 12 million by 1500. The information explosion. Reformation. Scientific Revolution. All from movable type.

nodes.label: Bronze Age (3300-1200 BC)
nodes.role: Copper + tin = bronze. Harder than either alone. The alloy that made tools, weapons, civilization. The first engineered material.

nodes.label: Iron Age (1200 BC - 600 AD)
nodes.role: Iron replaced bronze. Cheaper. More abundant. Democratized metal. The material that armed the masses.

nodes.label: Concrete (Roman, ~300 BC)
nodes.role: Romans invented concrete. The Pantheon still stands after 2,000 years. Modern concrete lasts 50. We forgot how to make it last.

nodes.label: Plastic (Bakelite, 1907)
nodes.role: Synthetic. Cheap. Everywhere. 8.3 billion tons produced. 79% in landfills or ocean. The material that outlives its creator by centuries.

nodes.label: Glass
nodes.role: Sand + heat = transparency. Lenses, telescopes, microscopes, fiber optics. Without glass, no science. The material that lets you see.

nodes.label: Graphene
nodes.role: One atom thick. 200x stronger than steel. Discovered with scotch tape (2004). Nobel 2010. The strongest material is the thinnest.

nodes.label: Steel
nodes.role: Iron + carbon. Bessemer process (1856). Skyscrapers, railways, bridges. The material that built the modern city.

nodes.label: Fire (~1 million years ago)
nodes.role: The first energy technology. Cooking. Warmth. Light. Protection. The commons of heat. Fire belongs to everyone.

nodes.label: Coal
nodes.role: Ancient forests compressed into rock. Powered the Industrial Revolution. 800,000 miners in 1920s US. Black lung. Child labor. The fuel that cost lives.

nodes.label: Oil / Petroleum
nodes.role: Ancient plankton compressed into liquid. Wars fought for it. Climate changed by it. The fuel that powers and destroys simultaneously.

nodes.label: Solar Energy
nodes.role: The sun sends 173,000 terawatts to Earth every second. We use 18. The energy is there. The infrastructure isn't. The commons overhead.

nodes.label: Wind Energy
nodes.role: Windmills since 500 AD. Denmark gets 50%+ from wind. The energy that's always been free. The infrastructure is the barrier.

nodes.label: Geothermal Energy
nodes.role: Earth's core is 5,400C. Iceland runs on it. The heat beneath your feet. The energy of the planet itself.

nodes.label: Gregorian Calendar (1582)
nodes.role: Pope Gregory XIII corrected the Julian calendar. 10 days vanished. October 4, 1582 was followed by October 15. The day the calendar jumped.

nodes.label: Time Zones (1884)
nodes.role: Before railroads, every town had its own time. Railroads needed schedules. 24 zones. GMT. Time standardized for commerce.

nodes.label: Leap Seconds
nodes.role: Earth's rotation is slowing. We add a second every few years. Time is not constant. The planet disagrees with the clock.

nodes.label: Deep Time (4.5 billion years)
nodes.role: If Earth's history is 24 hours: humans appear at 11:58:43 PM. All recorded history in the last 0.2 seconds. We are a blink.

nodes.label: Atomic Clock
nodes.role: Cesium-133 oscillates 9,192,631,770 times per second. The most precise measurement humans make. Time defined by counting atoms.

nodes.label: Barter
nodes.role: I have wheat, you have fish. Direct exchange. No money needed. The original economy. Works until you want something nobody nearby has.

nodes.label: Coinage (Lydia, ~600 BC)
nodes.role: King Croesus. Stamped metal. The state guarantees the value. Trust made physical. The first currency.

nodes.label: Paper Money (China, ~700 AD)
nodes.role: Song Dynasty. Promissory notes. The money that isn't metal. Trust made abstract. The original fiat currency.

nodes.label: Bitcoin (2009)
nodes.role: Satoshi Nakamoto. Decentralized. No central bank. Blockchain. Proof of work. The money that trusts math instead of institutions.

nodes.label: Gold Standard
nodes.role: Currency backed by gold. Nixon ended it (1971). Since then: money backed by... trust. The membrane removed.

nodes.label: Tulip Mania (1637)
nodes.role: A single tulip bulb cost more than a house. Then crashed. The first speculative bubble. The market as collective hallucination.

nodes.label: Nelson Mandela
nodes.role: 27 years in prison. Robben Island. Emerged without bitterness. Became president. The prisoner who outlasted the prison.

nodes.label: Alcatraz
nodes.role: The inescapable prison on an island. Closed 1963. Now a museum. The punishment that became a tourist attraction.

nodes.label: Mass Incarceration (US)
nodes.role: 2.3 million imprisoned. 25% of world's prisoners with 4% of population. $80 billion/year. The largest carceral system in human history.

nodes.label: 13th Amendment (1865)
nodes.role: Abolished slavery EXCEPT as punishment for a crime. The loophole that became mass incarceration. The exception that swallowed the rule.

nodes.label: Solitary Confinement
nodes.role: 23 hours alone. No human contact. UN says >15 days = torture. US prisoners spend years. The punishment that breaks the mind.

nodes.label: Restorative Justice
nodes.role: Not punishment. Repair. Victim and offender face each other. The community heals. The alternative to the cage.

nodes.label: French Revolution (1789)
nodes.role: Liberte, egalite, fraternite. Stormed the Bastille. Guillotined the king. Then guillotined each other. The revolution that ate itself.

nodes.label: Haitian Revolution (1791-1804)
nodes.role: Enslaved people defeated Napoleon's army. First successful slave revolt. Haiti punished for it for 200 years. The revolution the world never forgave.

nodes.label: Arab Spring (2010-2012)
nodes.role: One fruit vendor in Tunisia set himself on fire. Uprisings across 17 countries. Facebook organized it. Most revolutions failed. The network enabled and betrayed.

nodes.label: Mark Twain
nodes.role: 'The reports of my death are greatly exaggerated.' Satire as scalpel. Huck Finn. The humorist who told the truth by lying.

nodes.label: George Carlin
nodes.role: 'They call it the American Dream because you have to be asleep to believe it.' Seven dirty words. The comedian as philosopher.

nodes.label: Richard Pryor
nodes.role: Set himself on fire freebasing. Told the truth about race in America. Made people laugh at what should make them cry. The wound as punchline.

nodes.label: Jonathan Swift
nodes.role: A Modest Proposal (1729): eat Irish babies. Satire so savage people thought he was serious. The writer whose joke was the point.

nodes.label: A Modest Proposal (Swift, 1729)
nodes.role: 'Eat the children of the poor.' The satire that proposed the horror the system was already committing, just more honestly.

nodes.label: Dr. Seuss
nodes.role: The Lorax. The Sneetches. Horton Hears a Who. Environmental justice, class structure, and civil rights in rhyme. The teacher who used pictures.

nodes.label: Roald Dahl
nodes.role: Charlie and the Chocolate Factory. Matilda. James and the Giant Peach. Adults are cruel. Children are clever. The world through a child's eyes.

nodes.label: Maurice Sendak
nodes.role: Where the Wild Things Are. 'Let the wild rumpus start!' The book that said: children have rage and that's okay.

nodes.label: Fairy Tales (Original Versions)
nodes.role: Cinderella's stepsisters cut off their toes. Red Riding Hood was eaten. Snow White's queen danced in hot iron shoes. The originals were horror stories. Then Disney happened.

nodes.label: Triangle Shirtwaist Fire (1911)
nodes.role: 146 workers dead. Doors locked from outside. Jumped from 9th floor. Mostly young immigrant women. The fire that created workplace safety laws.

nodes.label: Child Labor
nodes.role: Children in mines, mills, factories. Lewis Hine's photographs (1908-1918) showed America what it was doing to its kids. The camera as conscience.

nodes.label: Lewis Hine
nodes.role: Photographed child laborers (1908-1918). His images led to child labor laws. The photographer who used evidence to protect children.

nodes.label: Eight-Hour Day Movement
nodes.role: 'Eight hours for work, eight hours for rest, eight hours for what we will.' Won through strikes, marches, death. The commons of time reclaimed.

nodes.label: Haymarket Affair (1886)
nodes.role: Chicago. Workers striking for 8-hour day. Bomb. Police fired into crowd. 4 labor leaders hanged. May Day exists because of this.

nodes.label: Cesar Chavez
nodes.role: United Farm Workers. Grape boycott. 'Si se puede.' The labor leader who organized the people everyone ignored.

nodes.label: Americans with Disabilities Act (1990)
nodes.role: Curb cuts, ramps, accessible buildings. The membrane expanded to include bodies the system excluded. The law that changed sidewalks.

nodes.label: Helen Keller
nodes.role: Deaf and blind from 19 months. Learned to read, write, speak. Graduated Radcliffe. Became a socialist activist. The story they teach is incomplete.

nodes.label: Curb Cut Effect
nodes.role: Curb cuts designed for wheelchairs help everyone: strollers, bikes, deliveries. The accommodation that improves the whole system. Universal design.

nodes.label: Death (The Concept)
nodes.role: The only certainty. Every culture has a name for it. Every religion has a theory about it. The one appointment everyone keeps.

nodes.label: Memento Mori
nodes.role: 'Remember you will die.' Roman slaves whispered it to generals during triumphs. The reminder that power is temporary.

nodes.label: Dia de los Muertos
nodes.role: Mexican tradition. The dead return for one night. Marigolds and sugar skulls. Death as reunion, not ending. The culture that invites the dead home.

nodes.label: Wakes and Funerals
nodes.role: Every culture gathers for the dead. The Irish wake. The New Orleans jazz funeral. The sitting shiva. The commons of grief.

nodes.label: Catacombs of Paris
nodes.role: 6 million skeletons. Moved underground when cemeteries overflowed (1786). The city built on its own dead. The foundation is bones.

nodes.label: Body Farms (Forensic Anthropology)
nodes.role: Fields where human bodies decompose for science. How flesh becomes soil. The dead teaching the living how to read death.

nodes.label: Death Masks
nodes.role: Plaster cast of the face after death. Newton, Beethoven, Lincoln, Napoleon. The last portrait. The face frozen at the end.

nodes.label: River Styx
nodes.role: Greek underworld river. Charon ferries the dead. You need a coin under your tongue to pay. Even death has a toll booth.

nodes.label: Valhalla
nodes.role: Norse afterlife for warriors. Die in battle, feast forever. Odin's hall. The reward for fighting, not winning.

nodes.label: Grim Reaper
nodes.role: Skeleton in a black robe with a scythe. European, 14th century. Born from the Black Death. The plague gave death a face.

nodes.label: Near-Death Experiences
nodes.role: Tunnel of light. Life review. Peace. Reported across cultures, religions, centuries. The brain's last story. Or the first truth.

nodes.label: Hospice / Palliative Care
nodes.role: Not cure. Comfort. The medicine that says: we cannot save you, but we can hold your hand. The dignity of the end.

nodes.label: Organ Donation
nodes.role: One donor can save 8 lives. The body that gives after death. The commons of flesh.

nodes.label: Ghost Stories (The Genre)
nodes.role: Every culture has them. The dead return because something is UNFINISHED. The ghost is the unresolved complaint.

nodes.label: Ghost of Hamlet's Father
nodes.role: Shakespeare. The murdered king returns to demand justice from his son. 'Remember me.' The dead demanding accountability.

nodes.label: William Shakespeare
nodes.role: Wrote Hamlet, Macbeth, Lear, Othello. Power, corruption, madness, jealousy. The human condition in iambic pentameter. Dead 400 years. Still the standard.

nodes.label: A Christmas Carol (Dickens, 1843)
nodes.role: Three ghosts show Scrooge his own cruelty. Past, Present, Future. The ghost story that's actually about accountability. Scrooge sees the evidence and changes.

nodes.label: Charles Dickens
nodes.role: Oliver Twist, Great Expectations, A Christmas Carol. Poverty, class, cruelty, redemption. The novelist who made England look at its own poor.

nodes.label: The Tell-Tale Heart (Poe, 1843)
nodes.role: The murderer hears the dead man's heartbeat under the floorboards. Confesses. The guilt that speaks. The evidence you can't bury.

nodes.label: Edgar Allan Poe
nodes.role: The Raven. The Tell-Tale Heart. The Masque of the Red Death. Invented the detective story. Died in a gutter at 40. Nobody knows how.

nodes.label: Ringu / The Ring (Japanese Horror)
nodes.role: A cursed videotape. Watch it, die in 7 days. The information that kills. The evidence that can't be unseen.

nodes.label: Bloody Mary (Urban Legend)
nodes.role: Say her name three times in a mirror. She appears. The ritual of summoning by speaking. Names have power.

nodes.label: Poltergeist
nodes.role: German: 'noisy ghost.' Objects move. Doors slam. The invisible force that disrupts. The disturbance you can't see but can't ignore.

nodes.label: Banshee (Irish)
nodes.role: Her wail announces death. You hear the scream before the loss. The warning that comes too late. The signal after the damage.

nodes.label: Yurei (Japanese Ghost)
nodes.role: White funeral clothes, long black hair, no feet. Returns because of unresolved grudge. Specifically: injustice. The Japanese ghost IS the unpunished wrong.

nodes.label: Duppy (Caribbean Ghost)
nodes.role: West African origin. Spirit of the dead that can be summoned or sent. Used in obeah. The dead as weapon. The ancestor weaponized.

nodes.label: La Llorona (The Weeping Woman)
nodes.role: Drowned her children. Wanders rivers weeping. Mexican/Latin American. The mother who destroyed what she loved. The guilt that walks forever.

nodes.label: Arachnophobia / Spiders
nodes.role: Most spiders are harmless. Fear is ancestral. 8 legs, 8 eyes, silk from the body. The weaver in the dark. The web you walk into.

nodes.label: Parasitic Wasps
nodes.role: Lay eggs inside living caterpillars. Larvae eat the host from inside. The host walks around alive while being consumed. Parasitism at its most literal.

nodes.label: Cordyceps (Zombie Fungus)
nodes.role: Infects ants. Takes over the brain. Walks the ant to the perfect spot. Kills it. Grows a stalk from the head. The parasite that puppets the host.

nodes.label: Vampire Bats
nodes.role: Drink blood. But: they share blood with hungry colony members who reciprocate later. The vampire that practices mutual aid.

nodes.label: Anglerfish
nodes.role: Deep sea. Bioluminescent lure. The light in the dark that attracts you IS the trap. The promise that eats.

nodes.label: Botfly
nodes.role: Lays eggs in human skin. Larva grows inside you. You feel it move. The organism that uses your body as a nursery.

nodes.label: Ticks
nodes.role: Wait on grass for years. Sense CO2. Climb on. Drink blood for days. Transmit Lyme disease. The patient parasite that gives you something worse.

nodes.label: Lampreys
nodes.role: Jawless fish. Circular mouth of teeth. Attaches to host, rasps through skin, drinks blood. 360 million years old. The original vampire.

nodes.label: Cuckoo (Brood Parasite)
nodes.role: Lays eggs in other birds' nests. Cuckoo chick pushes host's eggs out. Foster parents raise the imposter. The parasite raised as family.

nodes.label: Deathwatch Beetle
nodes.role: Taps inside walls at night. Sounds like a ticking clock. Associated with death vigils. The insect that counts down.

nodes.label: Sleep Paralysis
nodes.role: Awake but can't move. Often accompanied by a dark figure sitting on your chest. The demon is your own brain. The nightmare that's real.

nodes.label: Uncanny Valley
nodes.role: Almost-human faces trigger revulsion. Dolls, mannequins, bad CGI. The brain screams: WRONG. Too close to human but not human. The credential that's almost right.

nodes.label: Infrasound (Below 20 Hz)
nodes.role: Below human hearing. Causes anxiety, dread, chills, feeling of being watched. Produced by storms, machines, old buildings. Haunted houses have bad ventilation.

nodes.label: Will-o'-the-Wisp
nodes.role: Ghostly lights over marshes. Swamp gas igniting. Travelers follow the light into the bog and drown. The false signal that leads you to destruction.

nodes.label: Doppelganger
nodes.role: Your exact double. Seeing it means death. The copy that replaces you. The credential that mimics the real thing.

nodes.label: Wendigo (Algonquian)
nodes.role: Spirit of insatiable greed and hunger. Possesses humans who resort to cannibalism. The creature that eats and is never full. The extraction that never stops.

nodes.label: Skinwalker (Navajo)
nodes.role: Shapeshifter that wears the skin of animals. Taboo to speak of. The entity that uses another's identity. The stolen credential given form.

nodes.label: Changeling (European Folklore)
nodes.role: Fairies steal a human baby, leave a fairy child in its place. The parents raise the wrong child. The institution that replaced education with extraction.

nodes.label: Boogeyman / Bogeyman
nodes.role: The monster under the bed. Every culture has one. The fear that has no shape. The threat you can't see but won't let you sleep.

nodes.label: Witching Hour (3 AM)
nodes.role: The hour when the veil is thinnest. When ghosts walk. When the body is weakest. When the mind sees what daylight hides.

nodes.label: Mary Shelley
nodes.role: Wrote Frankenstein at 18 (1818). The monster isn't the creature. The monster is the creator who abandoned it. The first science fiction AND the first horror.

nodes.label: Frankenstein (Shelley, 1818)
nodes.role: A scientist creates life and runs away. The creature, abandoned, becomes violent. The horror is not the monster. The horror is the negligence.

nodes.label: Bram Stoker
nodes.role: Wrote Dracula (1897). The aristocrat who feeds on the poor. The parasite in a castle. The landlord with fangs.

nodes.label: Dracula (Stoker, 1897)
nodes.role: The count who drinks blood. Immortal. Aristocratic. Charming. Cannot enter unless invited. The extraction that requires your consent.

nodes.label: H.P. Lovecraft
nodes.role: Cosmic horror. Cthulhu. The universe is vast, indifferent, and incomprehensible. Also: deeply racist. The horror writer whose horror included his own worldview.

nodes.label: Cosmic Horror (Lovecraftian)
nodes.role: The universe doesn't care about you. Understanding the truth drives you insane. Knowledge as madness. The investigation that shows you what you can't unsee.

nodes.label: Shirley Jackson
nodes.role: The Lottery (1948). The Haunting of Hill House. Ordinary people doing monstrous things because tradition says so. The horror of compliance.

nodes.label: The Lottery (Jackson, 1948)
nodes.role: A small town stones one person to death every year. Because they always have. 'Lottery in June, corn be heavy soon.' The ritual murder that nobody questions.

nodes.label: Jordan Peele
nodes.role: Get Out. Us. Nope. Horror as racial commentary. The sunken place. The system that paralyzes while you watch.

nodes.label: Get Out (Peele, 2017)
nodes.role: White liberals kidnap Black people to steal their bodies. The sunken place: conscious but paralyzed. The liberal racism that smiles while it consumes.

nodes.label: Stephen King
nodes.role: It, The Shining, Carrie, Misery. Small-town evil. The monster is usually the community. The horror writer who found the monster in normalcy.

nodes.label: Genghis Khan (Temujin)
nodes.role: Born ~1162. Orphaned. Enslaved. United the Mongol tribes. Conquered from Korea to Hungary. Largest contiguous empire in history. 40 million killed. Also: religious tolerance, meritocracy, postal system, free trade. The destroyer who built.

nodes.label: Mongol Empire (1206-1368)
nodes.role: 24 million km2. 25% of world population. Pax Mongolica: the Silk Road's safest era. A merchant could walk from Korea to Hungary unmolested. The empire that made the network safe by terrifying everyone.

nodes.label: Kublai Khan
nodes.role: Genghis' grandson. Founded the Yuan Dynasty in China. Marco Polo visited his court. The conqueror who became the civilized ruler. The barbarian who built Beijing.

nodes.label: Pax Mongolica (1250-1350)
nodes.role: 100 years of Silk Road peace under Mongol protection. Trade, ideas, religion, and plague all flowed freely. The network secured by force. Also carried the Black Death to Europe.

nodes.label: Yasa (Mongol Law Code)
nodes.role: Genghis Khan's legal code. Religious freedom mandatory. Kidnapping = death. Adultery = death. Urinating in water = death. The law code of a man who was himself kidnapped as a child.

nodes.label: Yam (Mongol Postal System)
nodes.role: Relay stations every 25 miles across the empire. Riders could cover 200 miles/day. The original pony express. Communication at the speed of horse.

nodes.label: Genghis Khan's Genetic Legacy
nodes.role: ~16 million men alive today carry his Y-chromosome. 0.5% of all men on Earth. The most reproductively successful human in history. The conqueror is in the DNA.

nodes.label: Timur (Tamerlane)
nodes.role: Claimed descent from Genghis. Conquered from India to Turkey. Built towers of skulls. 17 million killed (5% of world population). The conqueror who made art from terror.

nodes.label: The Golden Horde
nodes.role: Mongol khanate that ruled Russia for 240 years (1240-1480). Russia was a Mongol vassal state for longer than America has existed. The occupation that shaped Russian identity.

nodes.label: Great Wall of China
nodes.role: 13,171 miles. Built over 2,000 years by multiple dynasties. Did NOT stop the Mongols (they went around it, bribed guards, or walked through gates left open). The wall that failed its purpose. History's most expensive security theater.

nodes.label: Qin Shi Huang (First Emperor)
nodes.role: United China (221 BC). Started the Great Wall. Burned books. Buried scholars alive. Built the terracotta army. The man who unified a nation by destroying its memory.

nodes.label: Terracotta Army (210 BC)
nodes.role: 8,000 clay soldiers buried with the First Emperor. Each face unique. An army for the afterlife. The monument to one man's refusal to die alone.

nodes.label: Berlin Wall (1961-1989)
nodes.role: Divided a city for 28 years. Families separated. 140 killed trying to cross. Fell Nov 9, 1989. David Hasselhoff sang. Walls fall.

nodes.label: Hadrian's Wall (122 AD)
nodes.role: 73 miles across northern England. Rome's edge. Beyond here: barbarians. The empire's boundary. The line between civilization and whatever we call the other side.

nodes.label: Dalai Lama (Institution)
nodes.role: Tibetan Buddhist leader. Each Dalai Lama is the reincarnation of the previous. The institution that survives by rebirth. The leader found, not elected.

nodes.label: 1st Dalai Lama: Gendun Drup (1391-1474)
nodes.role: Founded Tashilhunpo Monastery. Wasn't actually called 'Dalai Lama' during his lifetime — the title was applied retroactively. The founder who didn't know he was first.

nodes.label: 3rd Dalai Lama: Sonam Gyatso (1543-1588)
nodes.role: The one who actually received the title 'Dalai Lama' from Altan Khan of the Mongols (1578). 'Dalai' = Mongolian for 'ocean.' Ocean of wisdom. The Mongols named the institution.

nodes.label: 4th Dalai Lama: Yonten Gyatso (1589-1617)
nodes.role: The ONLY non-Tibetan Dalai Lama. Mongolian. Great-grandson of Altan Khan. The conqueror's bloodline became the spiritual leader. Politics as reincarnation.

nodes.label: 5th Dalai Lama: Ngawang Lobsang Gyatso (1617-1682)
nodes.role: 'The Great Fifth.' United Tibet under Dalai Lama rule. Built the Potala Palace. His death was hidden for 15 years to maintain stability. The leader whose death was a state secret.

nodes.label: 6th Dalai Lama: Tsangyang Gyatso (1683-1706)
nodes.role: The rebel Dalai Lama. Refused monastic vows. Wrote love poetry. Visited taverns. 'I dwell apart from the Potala... in the town.' Deposed and disappeared. The incarnation that refused the role.

nodes.label: 13th Dalai Lama: Thubten Gyatso (1876-1933)
nodes.role: Modernizer. Fled British invasion (1904), then Chinese invasion (1910). Declared Tibetan independence (1913). The Dalai Lama who tried to drag Tibet into the modern world.

nodes.label: 14th Dalai Lama: Tenzin Gyatso (born 1935)
nodes.role: Current Dalai Lama. Found at age 2 by search party using visions. Fled Tibet 1959. Nobel Peace Prize 1989. Has said the institution may end with him. The reincarnation that might choose not to return.

nodes.label: Potala Palace (Lhasa)
nodes.role: 1,000 rooms. 13 stories. Winter palace of the Dalai Lama since 1649. Built by the 5th. Now a museum under Chinese control. The throne without its occupant.

nodes.label: Panchen Lama Controversy
nodes.role: The Panchen Lama identifies the next Dalai Lama (and vice versa). China kidnapped the Dalai Lama's choice (Gedhun Choekyi Nyima, age 6, in 1995) and installed their own. The youngest political prisoner in the world. Now 37. Nobody has seen him since.

nodes.label: Gedhun Choekyi Nyima
nodes.role: Recognized as 11th Panchen Lama by the Dalai Lama at age 6 (1995). Kidnapped by Chinese government 3 days later. Never seen again. Now 37. The boy who disappeared because he was chosen.

nodes.label: Tulku System (Reincarnation Lineages)
nodes.role: Tibetan Buddhist system: enlightened teachers reborn deliberately. Search parties find the child. Tests confirm identity. The soul as institutional succession. The leader identified, not elected.

nodes.label: Chinese Occupation of Tibet (1950-present)
nodes.role: 1.2 million Tibetans killed. 6,000 monasteries destroyed. Cultural genocide ongoing. The Dalai Lama in exile since 1959. The commons of a civilization under occupation.
